name: Leningrad oblast
summary_text: This division carries one documented incident beyond the national pattern: in February 2025 a gender-nonconforming person who sold sex was murdered in a local town, dismembered and the remains dumped in the river in the region's principal city; the perpetrator was arrested within days and sentenced to 11 years in a strict-regime colony in September 2025 by the local city court. The case is recorded for the institutional response - swift arrest, prosecution and a substantial sentence - while press coverage mocked and misgendered the victim. The federal repression framework (anti-propaganda and extremism laws; for foreigners, detention of up to 15 days and deportation) otherwise applies unchanged in this division.

sources.title: Country policy and information note: sexual orientation and gender identity and expression, June 2025 (accessible) - GOV.UK
sources.claim_summary: UK Home Office country policy and information note on sexual orientation, gender identity and expression (June 2025): assesses that LGBT+ people outside the North Caucasus do not face a real risk from the state solely for sexual orientation, but trans people and active LGBT+ advocates are likely to face treatment amounting to persecution; at least 139 people were impacted by anti-LGBT+ laws 2022-2024 (propaganda-law convictions, detentions, 'extremism' prosecutions, fines and imprisonment).

NOTE: page not retrievable at fetch time (automated access blocked by the site); the underlying US State Department travel advisory for Russia warns all travellers regardless of personal characteristic (wrongful detention, arbitrary law enforcement) and notes foreigners found guilty under the propaganda law face arrest, up to 15 days' detention and deportation.

sources.title: Russia: Rising Toll of LGBT ‘Extremism’ Designation | Human Rights Watch
sources.claim_summary: Human Rights Watch news report (30 June 2025) on the rising toll of LGBT 'extremism' designations: Russian courts have issued over 100 convictions for participation in the designated 'International LGBT Movement' or displaying its alleged symbols, and authorities are weaponising the justice system to enforce it.
